_comment: The statues and reliefs in the corridor and atrium. Read by src/core/Sculpture.cpp.
place: "atrium" stands it under the oculus; "niche 0" to "niche 3" are the corridor niches in plan.json.
height is the statue alone, in metres. plinth is width, height and depth.
turn spins a scan that does not face the visitor; forward moves it out of the niche, in metres.
about is a line for the label: where and when it was made.
wall is the outer face of the atrium a relief hangs on; at is plan x for N and S, plan y for E and W.
Every credit here is shown on the credits screen (F3). See assets/CREDITS.md.

statues.title: Apollo Belvedere
statues.about: Roman marble, about 120 to 140 CE, after a Greek bronze by Leochares
statues.credit: Apollo Belvedere by Rigsters, CC BY 4.0, sketchfab.com/rigsters

statues.title: Demeter of Knidos
statues.about: Greek marble, about 350 BCE, from Knidos. The original is in the British Museum
statues.credit: Demeter of Knidos by Bonn Center for Digital Humanities, CC BY 4.0, sketchfab.com/bcdh

statues.title: Maya and Merit
statues.about: Egyptian limestone, about 1320 BCE. Maya was treasurer to Tutankhamun
statues.credit: Maya and Merit, National Museum of Antiquities, Leiden, CC0

statues.title: Zeus or Poseidon of Artemision
statues.about: Greek bronze, about 460 BCE, found in the sea off Cape Artemision
statues.credit: Zeus or Poseidon from the Artemision, SMK National Gallery of Denmark, CC0

statues.title: Discobolus

statues.credit: Discobolus, SMK National Gallery of Denmark, CC0
